question: WHAT MAKES
THIS WORK?
recap: A train in a curve: both wheels sit on one solid axle and always turn at the same speed.
explain: Train wheels are not flat – they are slightly cone-shaped, wider on the inside next to the flange.
In a curve the axle shifts outward, so the outer wheel rolls on a bigger diameter and covers more distance per turn than the inner wheel.
That steers the train around the bend by itself. Most wheels have a taper of about 1 in 20 – the flanges are only a last line of defence.
